title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: TASHA'S SONG
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Tasha Bell, an airport security screener in Pensacola, Florida.
All day, she tells strangers to take off their shoes.
But ask her to sing in public, and she'd rather go through the scanner herself.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SPEECH
segments.quote: The bitterest tears shed over graves are for words left unsaid and deeds left undone.
segments.author: Harriet Beecher Stowe
lines: Her mom, Gloria, was turning sixty, with a party at the VFW hall.
Tasha planned a speech. Thanks, Mom. Cake's over there.
Then she saw an old card on Mom's fridge, from Harriet Beecher Stowe:
The bitterest tears shed over graves are for words left unsaid and deeds left undone.
Mom sang in that kitchen every morning. So Tasha decided to sing for her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: OPEN MIC NIGHT
segments.quote: Mistakes are a fact of life. It is the response to the error that counts.
segments.author: Nikki Giovanni
lines: To get ready, she tried karaoke night at the Shrimp Shack.
Her voice cracked so hard, a man asked if the smoke alarm went off.
In the parking lot, her friend Nia texted her a line from the poet Nikki Giovanni:
Mistakes are a fact of life. It is the response to the error that counts.
Tasha walked back in and signed up for next Thursday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: HER OWN VOICE
segments.quote: Music is your own experience, your thoughts, your wisdom. If you don't live it, it won't come out of your horn.
segments.author: Charlie Parker
lines: Nia sent her to Mister Lamar, who sang in a Navy band for thirty years.
Tasha copied the famous record, every trill. Mister Lamar winced, and pointed to a photo of Charlie Parker:
Music is your own experience, your thoughts, your wisdom. If you don't live it, it won't come out of your horn.
So she sang it like Mom did, over the pancakes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BREAK ROOM
segments.quote: The most perfect technique is that which is not noticed at all.
segments.author: Pablo Casals
lines: She practiced in the car, and in the airport break room.
But she thought about her breathing so hard, she forgot the song.
Mister Lamar quoted the cellist Pablo Casals:
The most perfect technique is that which is not noticed at all.
So she drilled it every day, until she didn't have to think.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE STORM
segments.quote: There's nothing remarkable about it. All one has to do is hit the right keys at the right time and the instrument plays itself.
segments.author: Johann Sebastian Bach
lines: Party night. Big Florida thunderstorm. Halfway through the intro, the power went out.
Mister Lamar laughed and called out a line from Bach:
There's nothing remarkable about it. All one has to do is hit the right keys at the right time and the instrument plays itself.
So Tasha sang in the dark, with no music. By the second verse, Mom sang with her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE ENCORE
segments.quote: The only thing better than singing is more singing.
segments.author: Ella Fitzgerald
lines: When the lights came back, the hall was on its feet. Uncle Ray cried into the potato salad.
Mom hugged her and whispered a line from Ella Fitzgerald:
The only thing better than singing is more singing.
Now they sing a duet at the Shrimp Shack every month. The smoke alarm man claps loudest.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Say it now. Answer your mistakes. Use your own voice. Practice. Keep going. Sing more.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say it now. Answer your mistakes. Use your own voice. Practice. Keep going in the dark. Sing more.
I sing in the shower too. My neighbors call it the weather report.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
